changes: Karṇadeva: the compound karṇadevopādhyāya means 'the teacher (upādhyāya) of Karṇadeva', an epithet of the author Vardhamāna. It is not Karṇadeva's own title and not a father's name. Role changed from relative_only to other; title upādhyāya moved to Vardhamāna.
Relation changed from Vardhamāna son_of Karṇadeva to Karṇadeva pupil_of Vardhamāna.
Commissioner p3: name 'Unknown' replaced by an empty string because the name is lost in the lacuna. The evidence was shortened.
Purpose rewritten: the copy was made for someone's benefit (name lost) and for the benefit of others (parārtha).
Notes: removed the unverified exact weekday equivalence (Thursday, 31 October 1532). Added notes on the lacuna and the era.

purpose: for the benefit of the (lost-named) commissioner and paropakārārtha (for others)
notes: I read 'karṇadevopādhyāya' as an epithet of Vardhamāna, meaning 'preceptor of (king) Karṇadeva'. Karṇadeva has nothing to do with this copy. The commissioner's personal name is lost; only the title miśra survives. '..kapakarārthaṃ' is probably a corrupted '...-sya upakārārthaṃ' (for the benefit of [name]), and 'liṣāpitaṃ' stands for likhāpitaṃ. The era is not stated; reading 'saṃvat' as Vikrama gives 1532 CE (Śaka would give 1667 CE, which is less likely). The weekday has not been checked.
